title: São Tomé and Príncipe calculator readiness evidence — Batch 59
scope_note: This is an evidence refresh, not a readiness certification or calculator data file. National and secondary indicators must not be mistaken for district yields, farmgate prices or farmer-paid costs.

findings.production: Secondary FAOSTAT-derived 2024 national totals: maize 796 t; cassava 1,434 t; bananas 5,374 t; cocoa beans 4,000 t; palm oil 4,870 t; coffee 7 t. These require direct FAOSTAT/INE table verification and matching harvested area before yield calculation.
findings.cocoa: FAO says cocoa dominates exports. The EC value-chain study gives historical 2017 production and plantation area and explains conventional/certified cooperative channels. Do not use historical 2017 figures as current productivity or budgets.
findings.geography: INE confirms 7 districts; Pagué is the sole district on Príncipe, an autonomous region. Island/district lookup is known, but crop-specific production-zone mapping is not validated.
findings.seasonality: INE describes a long wet season roughly September-June and a drier Gravana June-September; local terrain creates microclimatic variation. Do not infer uniform planting calendars or yields across districts.
findings.market_prices: July 2026 tomato quote STN120-130/kg is a consumer/market price reported in a news interview, not a farmgate observation. May 2026 cocoa export unit value STN64.37/kg is customs value, not producer price. They are context only and must not feed calculator revenue.
findings.census: The 2025 General Agricultural Census is listed in FAO's WCA catalogue. INE phase-2 reporting in May 2026 describes a complementary survey to establish actual production. A complete public crop-by-district final table was not verified in this review.
findings.inputs: No current farmer-paid, dated and district-specific price schedule was verified for seed/planting material, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, machinery, irrigation/water/energy, transport or post-harvest processing.
findings.currency: Use STN new dobra; verify current central-bank rate policy and local price-unit conventions before any foreign-currency conversion. Do not confuse older STD denomination with STN.

sources.name: FAO country overview
sources.finding: Agriculture employs more than 65% of the population per FAO's country overview; cocoa dominates exports (FAO overview describes about 90% of exports). Small domestic market and limited diversification are structural constraints.

sources.name: INE country profile and administrative geography
sources.finding: INE confirms seven districts: Água Grande, Cantagalo, Caué, Lembá, Lobata, Mé-Zóchi and Pagué; Pagué is on Príncipe, which has autonomous-region status. Two main islands, volcanic terrain and nine-month wet season (September-June) plus Gravana (June-September).

sources.name: FAO WCA round 2020 catalogue
sources.finding: FAO catalogue identifies São Tomé and Príncipe's 2025 agricultural census and lists questionnaires, but no final report/tables in the catalogue view reviewed.

sources.name: INE phase 2 census reporting
sources.finding: 14 May 2026 report quotes INE census leadership saying phase 2 is a complementary survey to determine actual national production after identifying active agricultural operators. This indicates detailed production collection was still underway at that point.

sources.name: FAOSTAT-derived crop production summary
sources.finding: Secondary FAOSTAT-based summary lists 2024 production: maize 796 t, cassava 1,434 t, bananas 5,374 t, cocoa beans 4,000 t, palm oil 4,870 t and coffee 7 t. These are national totals only; area, district yields and source-table validation not extracted.

sources.name: Cocoa value-chain analysis (European Commission)
sources.finding: 2017 baseline: cocoa plantations about 25,000 ha; 2,488 t conventional and 1,065 t certified cocoa. Report identifies production zones on São Tomé, small-producer/cooperative channels and post-harvest fermentation/drying. Historical, not current yield/cost schedule.

sources.name: WFP country strategic plan 2024-2028
sources.finding: WFP describes export-crop orientation, cocoa-led exports, small domestic market, infrastructure and cold-storage constraints; structural context only.

sources.name: Tomato market price report
sources.finding: 12 July 2026 consumer interview reports tomatoes at STN 120-130/kg at market/consumer level; farmer-platform representative attributes price pressure to reduced production and climate conditions. Not a farmgate quote and not a representative market series.

sources.name: Cocoa export unit value
sources.finding: Secondary page reports May 2026 UN Comtrade export unit value 64.37 STN/kg. Customs/export unit value, not farmgate; not usable as producer revenue.

sources.name: Trade/FAOSTAT crop context
sources.finding: US trade guide (2022) describes cocoa, palm oil, chocolate, pepper, coconut oil and coffee as agricultural export activities and identifies horticulture/fruit value-chain potential; dated context only.

blockers: Obtain and extract the complete 2025 General Agricultural Census phase-2 report and crop-by-district tables; reconcile any 2026 headline totals to the primary report.
Download direct FAOSTAT crop area and production series for STP; reconcile national output and crop-year definitions with INE before deriving yields.
Obtain dated producer/farmgate prices by crop, grade, transaction level, district/island and unit; exclude consumer tomato prices and cocoa customs unit values from farm revenue.
Obtain current farmer-paid seed, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, machinery, land preparation, irrigation, water, energy, transport, drying and fermentation costs.

Construct separate cocoa establishment and mature-orchard budgets, including cooperative/certification and post-harvest pathways; build annual food-crop budgets for maize, cassava, banana and horticulture.
Validate island/district crop calendars and production systems; do not assign national yields uniformly to seven districts.
Confirm current BCSTP currency and exchange-rate conventions, then build STN regression tests.
decision: Keep São Tomé and Príncipe inactive. Evidence refresh improves source discovery and national context but does not meet the farmgate-price, input-cost, regional-budget or test-case requirements.
next_step: Extract the final census tables and direct FAOSTAT area/output series; then collect district farmgate prices and farmer-paid input quotations before constructing enterprise budgets.
